title: Coulomb's law: force against distance
caption: $q_1=1\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ and $q_2=2\,\mu\mathrm{C}$. On log-log axes the force is a straight line of slope $-2$: doubling the distance divides the force by four. At $10\,\mathrm{cm}$ it is $1.8\,\mathrm{N}$.

title: Net force on a test charge near two fixed charges
caption: $q_1=+2\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ at $x=0$, $q_2=-3\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ at $x=0.10\,\mathrm{m}$, test charge $+1\,\mu\mathrm{C}$. The force is repulsive near $q_1$, attractive near $q_2$ and passes through zero once, at $x=-0.445\,\mathrm{m}$ (outside, on the side of the weaker charge).

title: Superposition of forces: the fourth corner of a square
caption: Charges $+2\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ at three corners of a square of side $0.30\,\mathrm{m}$ act on a fourth $+2\,\mu\mathrm{C}$: two forces of $0.40\,\mathrm{N}$ along the sides and one of $0.20\,\mathrm{N}$ along the diagonal. Resultant $0.765\,\mathrm{N}$ along the diagonal.

title: Electric field lines of a dipole
caption: $\pm1\,\mathrm{nC}$ at $x=\pm1\,\mathrm{cm}$. Lines leave the positive charge and end on the negative one; the field is strongest between and next to the charges, and at the midpoint it equals $2kq/a^2=1.8\times10^5\,\mathrm{N/C}$.
formula: \vec E=k\sum_i q_i\frac{\vec r-\vec r_i}{|\vec r-\vec r_i|^3}

title: Field on the axis of a charged ring
caption: $Q=5\,\mathrm{nC}$, $R=6\,\mathrm{cm}$: zero at the centre, a maximum at $z=R/\sqrt2=4.24\,\mathrm{cm}$ and an inverse-square tail $kQ/z^2$ far away. At $z=8\,\mathrm{cm}$ the field is $3.6\times10^3\,\mathrm{N/C}$.

title: How the field falls with distance for three charge distributions
caption: Point charge $E\propto1/r^2$, long line of charge $E\propto1/r$, large sheet $E=\text{const}$. Log-log slopes: $-2$, $-1$ and $0$. (Each uses $1\,\mathrm{nC}$, $1\,\mathrm{nC/m}$ and $1\,\mathrm{nC/m^2}$.)

title: On the axis of a dipole: exact field and the far-field law
caption: Charges $\pm q$ separated by $2a$: the exact axial field tends to $2kp/z^3$ (inverse cube) once $z\gg a$; the two curves differ by 2 % at $z=10a$ and by less than $1\,\%$ beyond $z=15a$.

title: Field of a charged sphere: insulating ball and conducting shell
caption: Total charge $Q=10\,\mathrm{nC}$, radius $R=5\,\mathrm{cm}$. Outside, both give $kQ/r^2$. Inside the uniform ball $E=kQr/R^3$ grows linearly; inside the conductor the field is zero (all the charge sits on the surface).
formula: \oint\vec E\cdot d\vec A=\frac{Q_{\rm enc}}{\varepsilon_0}\ \Rightarrow\ E=\frac{kQ}{r^2}\ (r>R),\quad E=\frac{kQr}{R^3}\ (r<R,\ \text{uniform ball})

title: Electric flux through a flat surface against its orientation
caption: Uniform field $E=500\,\mathrm{N/C}$ and area $A=0.20\,\mathrm{m^2}$: $\Phi=EA\cos\theta$ with $\theta$ the angle between $\vec E$ and the normal. Maximum $100\,\mathrm{N\,m^2/C}$ face-on, zero edge-on, negative when the normal points against the field.

title: Field of infinite charged sheets (superposition)
caption: Each sheet gives $\sigma/2\varepsilon_0$ pointing away from it (if positive). Opposite sheets $\pm\sigma$: the fields add between them ($\sigma/\varepsilon_0$) and cancel outside. Equal sheets: the opposite.

title: Field of a long uniformly charged cylinder
caption: Charge per length $\lambda=2\,\mathrm{nC/m}$, radius $R=2\,\mathrm{cm}$: inside $E=\lambda r/(2\pi\varepsilon_0R^2)$ (linear), outside $E=\lambda/(2\pi\varepsilon_0r)$ (inverse), continuous at the surface.

title: Equipotentials of a dipole and the field they imply
caption: Equipotentials (colour, labelled in volts) are perpendicular to the field lines; the field points from high to low potential. Here $\pm1\,\mathrm{nC}$ at $x=\pm1\,\mathrm{cm}$ and the mid-plane is at $0\,\mathrm{V}$.

title: Potential of a charged sphere: point charge, insulating ball, conductor
caption: $Q=10\,\mathrm{nC}$, $R=5\,\mathrm{cm}$. Outside, $V=kQ/r$ for all three. A conductor is an equipotential ($kQ/R=1800\,\mathrm{V}$); inside a uniform ball $V=\frac{kQ}{2R}\left(3-r^2/R^2\right)$, reaching $2700\,\mathrm{V}$ at the centre.

title: Potential on the axis of a ring and of a disk
caption: Both have the same total charge ($5\,\mathrm{nC}$) and radius ($6\,\mathrm{cm}$). The ring: $V=kQ/\sqrt{z^2+R^2}$. The disk: $V=\frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(\sqrt{z^2+R^2}-z\right)$. Far away both tend to $kQ/z$; $E_z=-dV/dz$.

title: Electric potential energy of two point charges
caption: For $q_1q_2>0$ (repulsion) $U$ is positive and falls to zero at infinity; for $q_1q_2<0$ (attraction) it is negative: $-U$ is the energy needed to separate the pair. Here $|q_1q_2|=2\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{C^2}$.

title: Charged particles in a uniform magnetic field
caption: $B=0.05\,\mathrm{T}$ into the page, both particles at $10^5\,\mathrm{m/s}$: a proton goes round a circle of radius $mv/(eB)=2.1\,\mathrm{cm}$; an alpha particle (twice the charge, four times the mass) a circle twice as big, in the same sense. The period $2\pi m/(qB)$ does not depend on the speed.

title: Helical motion: velocity components along and across the field
caption: An electron with $v_\perp=3\times10^6\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $v_\parallel=1\times10^6\,\mathrm{m/s}$ in $B=2\,\mathrm{mT}$: a circle of radius $r=mv_\perp/(eB)$ in the plane perpendicular to $\vec B$ combined with uniform motion along $\vec B$; the pitch is $p=v_\parallel T$.

title: Hall voltage against the magnetic field
caption: A strip $0.5\,\mathrm{mm}$ thick carrying $10\,\mathrm{A}$: $V_H=IB/(net)$ is linear in $B$, and tiny for a metal (copper) but thousands of times larger for a semiconductor with few carriers; that is why Hall probes use semiconductors.

title: Torque and potential energy of a current loop in a field
caption: A coil with $\mu=NIA=2\,\mathrm{A\,m^2}$ in $B=0.30\,\mathrm{T}$: the torque $\tau=\mu B\sin\phi$ is largest ($0.6\,\mathrm{N\,m}$) when the plane is parallel to $\vec B$; the potential energy $U=-\mu B\cos\phi$ is lowest when $\vec\mu\parallel\vec B$ (the torque is the slope of $U$, $\tau=dU/d\phi$).

title: Magnetic field inside and outside a long straight wire
caption: $I=10\,\mathrm{A}$ spread uniformly over a wire of radius $2\,\mathrm{mm}$: inside $B=\mu_0Ir/(2\pi R^2)$ rises linearly, outside $B=\mu_0I/(2\pi r)$ falls as $1/r$; the peak $1\,\mathrm{mT}$ is at the surface.

title: A single loop against a Helmholtz pair
caption: Two identical loops of radius $R$ a distance $R$ apart give an almost uniform field near the centre: the first and second derivatives of $B$ vanish there, so the variation within $\pm0.2R$ is under $0.5\,\%$ (a single loop varies by about $10\,\%$).
formula: B_{\rm loop}(z)=\frac{\mu_0IR^2}{2(R^2+z^2)^{3/2}},\qquad B_{\rm pair}=B_{\rm loop}(z-\tfrac R2)+B_{\rm loop}(z+\tfrac R2)

title: Field on the axis of a finite solenoid
caption: $n=2000$ turns per metre, $I=1.5\,\mathrm{A}$, length $0.30\,\mathrm{m}$, radius $2\,\mathrm{cm}$. In the middle $B\approx\mu_0nI=3.77\,\mathrm{mT}$ (the ideal value); at each end it falls to about half of that.

title: Force between parallel currents
caption: $F/L=\mu_0I_1I_2/(2\pi d)$: inversely proportional to the separation (slope $-1$ on log-log axes) and proportional to the product of the currents; $1.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{N/m}$ for $10\,\mathrm{A}$ and $10\,\mathrm{A}$ at $2\,\mathrm{cm}$. Parallel currents attract.

title: Faraday's law: flux and induced emf
caption: A coil of $N=200$ turns in a field whose flux through one turn is $\Phi=\Phi_0\sin\omega t$ ($\Phi_0=2\,\mathrm{mWb}$, $f=50\,\mathrm{Hz}$). The emf $-N\,d\Phi/dt$ is a cosine: largest when the flux is zero and zero when the flux is at its peak; its amplitude is $N\omega\Phi_0=126\,\mathrm{V}$.

title: Growth and decay of the current in an RL circuit
caption: $\varepsilon=12\,\mathrm{V}$, $R=24\,\Omega$, $L=0.60\,\mathrm{H}$: $\tau=L/R=25\,\mathrm{ms}$. The current reaches $63\,\%$ of $\varepsilon/R=0.5\,\mathrm{A}$ at $t=\tau$ and is $37\,\%$ of its initial value one time constant after the battery is removed. The stored energy is $\tfrac12LI^2$.

title: Motional emf: a sliding rod is braked by its own induced current
caption: A rod ($m=0.10\,\mathrm{kg}$, $l=0.40\,\mathrm{m}$) slides on rails closed through $R=0.30\,\Omega$ in $B=0.50\,\mathrm{T}$ with initial speed $6\,\mathrm{m/s}$. The magnetic force $B^2l^2v/R$ opposes the motion: $v=v_0e^{-t/\tau}$ with $\tau=mR/(B^2l^2)=0.75\,\mathrm{s}$; all the initial kinetic energy ends as heat in $R$.

title: Energy stored in an inductor
caption: $U=\tfrac12LI^2$ grows with the square of the current and in proportion to the inductance. The same coil that stores $0.075\,\mathrm{J}$ at $0.5\,\mathrm{A}$ ($L=0.6\,\mathrm{H}$) stores four times as much at $1\,\mathrm{A}$.

title: Induced electric field of a changing solenoid field
caption: $R=5\,\mathrm{cm}$, $dB/dt=0.020\,\mathrm{T/s}$: inside the solenoid $E=\tfrac r2\,dB/dt$ grows linearly ($3.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{V/m}$ at $3\,\mathrm{cm}$); outside it falls as $R^2/(2r)\,dB/dt$ ($2.5\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{V/m}$ at $10\,\mathrm{cm}$), although $B=0$ there.

title: A plane electromagnetic wave
caption: $\vec E$ and $\vec B$ are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, and they are in phase; their amplitudes are tied by $E_0=cB_0$. With $E_0=150\,\mathrm{V/m}$ the magnetic amplitude is $5.0\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{T}$.

title: Refraction and total internal reflection
caption: Air to glass ($n=1.5$): the ray bends towards the normal; $40^\circ$ becomes $25.4^\circ$. Glass to air: the ray bends away, and beyond the critical angle $\theta_c=\sin^{-1}(1/1.5)=41.8^\circ$ there is no refracted ray (total internal reflection).

title: Polarizers: Malus's law and the middle polarizer
caption: Left: unpolarized light through one polarizer gives $I_0/2$; a second polarizer at angle $\theta$ gives $\tfrac12I_0\cos^2\theta$. Right: crossed polarizers pass nothing, but a third one at $45^\circ$ between them restores $I_0/8$: $I=\tfrac18I_0\sin^22\theta$.

title: Dispersion: refractive index and prism deviation against wavelength
caption: Glass bends short wavelengths more than long ones (Cauchy fit $n=A+B/\lambda^2$ for crown glass). For a $60^\circ$ prism the minimum deviation is $\delta=2\sin^{-1}(n\sin30^\circ)-60^\circ$: about $39.4^\circ$ for violet and $37.8^\circ$ for red.

title: Thin lens: image distance and magnification against object distance
caption: $f=10\,\mathrm{cm}$ converging lens. Object beyond $f$: a real inverted image ($s'>0$, $m<0$), at infinity when $s\to f^+$ and at $2f$ when $s=2f$ (then $m=-1$). Object inside $f$: a virtual, upright, enlarged image ($s'<0$, $m>1$).

title: Ray diagram of a converging lens
caption: Object $3\,\mathrm{cm}$ high, $25\,\mathrm{cm}$ from a lens with $f=10\,\mathrm{cm}$. The three principal rays (parallel → through the far focus; through the centre → straight; through the near focus → parallel) meet at $s'=16.7\,\mathrm{cm}$ giving an inverted image $m=-0.67$ ($2\,\mathrm{cm}$ high).

title: Spherical mirrors: image distance against object distance
caption: A concave mirror with $f=15\,\mathrm{cm}$ forms real images beyond $f$ (inverted) and virtual ones inside $f$; a convex mirror ($f=-15\,\mathrm{cm}$) always gives a virtual, upright, reduced image between the mirror and its focus.

title: Lensmaker's equation: focal length of a biconvex lens
caption: For a thin lens in air $1/f=(n-1)(1/R_1-1/R_2)$. Left: a symmetric biconvex lens with $n=1.5$ has $f=R$. Right: for $R_1=-R_2=20\,\mathrm{cm}$ a higher refractive index gives a shorter focal length.

title: Double-slit interference pattern
caption: $d=0.20\,\mathrm{mm}$, $\lambda=600\,\mathrm{nm}$, screen at $2.0\,\mathrm{m}$: bright fringes where $d\sin\theta=m\lambda$, spaced by $\Delta y=\lambda L/d=6.0\,\mathrm{mm}$; between them the intensity falls to zero (ideal slits of negligible width).

title: Fringe spacing depends on the wavelength
caption: The same double slit ($d=0.20\,\mathrm{mm}$, $L=2.0\,\mathrm{m}$) with red ($650\,\mathrm{nm}$), green ($530\,\mathrm{nm}$) and blue ($450\,\mathrm{nm}$) light: $\Delta y=\lambda L/d$, so red fringes are the widest and all colours coincide at the central maximum (white light gives a white centre and coloured edges).

title: Anti-reflection coating: reflectance against film thickness
caption: A MgF$_2$ film ($n=1.38$) on glass ($n=1.50$) in air, light of $550\,\mathrm{nm}$. Both reflections invert the wave, so the two beams cancel (as far as their different amplitudes allow) when $2nt=(m+\tfrac12)\lambda$: the first minimum is at $t=\lambda/4n=99.6\,\mathrm{nm}$, where the reflectance falls from $4\,\%$ (bare glass) to $1.4\,\%$.

title: Superposition of two waves: the phase difference decides the amplitude
caption: Two waves of amplitude $A$ with phase difference $\varphi$ add to a wave of amplitude $2A|\cos(\varphi/2)|$: $2A$ when in phase, $\sqrt2A$ for $\varphi=90^\circ$, zero when they are opposite ($\varphi=180^\circ$).

title: Single-slit diffraction
caption: $I=I_0\,[\sin\beta/\beta]^2$ with $\beta=\pi a\sin\theta/\lambda$; minima at $a\sin\theta=m\lambda$ ($m=\pm1,\pm2,\dots$). A narrower slit gives a wider central maximum, whose full width is $2\lambda/a$ in $\sin\theta$; the side maxima are only $4.7\,\%$ and $1.65\,\%$ of the central one.

title: Double slit with slits of finite width: interference × diffraction
caption: $d=3a$: the narrow interference fringes ($\cos^2$) sit under the single-slit envelope ($\mathrm{sinc}^2$). The orders $m=\pm3,\pm6,\dots$ fall exactly on the zeros of the envelope and are missing; 5 fringes fit in the central maximum.

title: Diffraction gratings: more slits, sharper maxima
caption: Intensity for $N=2$, $5$ and $20$ slits of the same spacing $d$. The principal maxima ($d\sin\theta=m\lambda$) stay where they are but their width shrinks as $1/N$, and $N-2$ weak secondary maxima appear between them.

title: Circular aperture: the Airy pattern and the Rayleigh criterion
caption: $I=I_0\,[2J_1(x)/x]^2$ with $x=\pi D\sin\theta/\lambda$; the first dark ring is at $x=3.832$, i.e. $\sin\theta=1.22\lambda/D$. Two equal incoherent sources that far apart are just resolved: the dip between their peaks is about $26\,\%$.

title: Bragg reflection of X-rays
caption: Crystal planes $0.282\,\mathrm{nm}$ apart: constructive reflection when $2d\sin\theta=m\lambda$. For $\lambda=0.154\,\mathrm{nm}$ the first order is at $15.8^\circ$; shorter wavelengths give smaller angles and higher orders appear when $\lambda\le2d/m$.
